about: Distances read by the player on the in-game galaxy map (LJ = Lichtjahre = light years), collected to find how the game places systems inside a region and how many light years one region (voxel) step is. Append new samples; keep the context (galaxy map open?, camera focus) - the gGalacticScale value is the map camera's focus, not necessarily the current system.

known_positions_voxels.note: Positions in region units (1 unit = 400 LJ, confirmed by the centre distance). Only values read with the map camera locked on the star are trusted: with the map closed the value keeps the camera's last focus, not the current system. CAUTION 2026-10-05 14:30: the user saw the map's centre distance change with the viewport - the gGalacticScale value is the camera's position, so a 'locked' reading is a star's position only if the camera sits exactly on it; positions identified by matching the centre distance are camera positions.

2026-10-05 14:35: user: locking zooms the camera toward the star; rotating changes the centre distance; the viewport differs each time. So gGalacticScale = the camera EYE position (orbiting the locked star at a zoom radius), not the star. All 'locked' positions logged today are eye positions = star + offset.

2026-10-05: neighbouring galaxy-shader parameters: gTracePDX, gTracePDY (camera basis), gGoalCenterDir (= normalize(-eye): direction to the core), gInterest, gScreen, gIterations, gSunCore*, gBG* - no look-at target. Plan: orbit fit - while orbiting a locked star the eye stays on a sphere whose centre is the star (orbit_logger logs every change; needs horizontal AND vertical rotation, else only a circle).
2026-10-05: the user cannot rotate a locked camera (manual rotation moves it). Lock flights are curved; lock end points of one star differ by up to 130 LJ: end points are not star positions.

2026-10-05: camera block in memory = gTracePDX (screen right half-axis), gTracePDY (screen down half-axis; |PDX|/|PDY| = 1.773 = gScreen aspect 2240/1264, dot ~ 0), gGoalCenterDir, gGalacticScale (eye, x100). Viewing direction = normalize(cross(PDX, PDY)) (sign to be checked). A locked star is at the screen centre: star on the line eye + t * forward; two locks from different directions -> line intersection = star. ray_logger logs eye + PDX + PDY.
